title: Count The Repetitions
summary: Given strings s1 and s2, and integers n1 and n2, where str1 is s1 repeated n1 times and str2 is s2 repeated n2 times, find the largest integer m such that str2 repeated m times can be derived from str1 by removing some characters.
statement: Given strings s1 and s2, and integers n1 and n2, where str1 is s1 repeated n1 times and str2 is s2 repeated n2 times, find the largest integer m such that str2 repeated m times can be derived from str1 by removing some characters.
constraints: 1 <= len(s1), len(s2) <= 100; lowercase English letters only; 1 <= n1,n2 <= 1,000,000.
Find the largest m such that s2 repeated n2*m times is a subsequence of s1 repeated n1 times.
Matching characters need not be contiguous and may cross source-block boundaries. Return a count, not the expanded strings.
hints: After a source block, future matching depends only on the next character needed in s2.
Record the target offset and completed target copies at each source-block boundary.
When an offset repeats, compute the block period and match gain, skip whole periods, then scan the short remainder.
Greedy subsequence matching maximizes completed target copies; divide that number by n2 only after all source blocks.
editorial: Matching the earliest available character never harms a later subsequence completion. There are only len(s2) boundary offsets. A repeated offset means subsequent source blocks repeat the same transition cycle and target-copy gain, so whole cycles can be skipped arithmetically. The unmatched prefix must survive source-block boundaries. At most O(len(s2)) blocks need literal scanning before cycle skipping and the final remainder; no million-fold string expansion is needed. The oracle independently searches expanded small targets in small sources.

tests.explanation: Each acb supplies one subsequence ab. Four ab matches form two groups of (ab repeated twice), so return 2.
In ababab, baba is a subsequence crossing block boundaries. Two ba copies fit, but a third lacks a final a.
